title: Finite complex construction: simultaneous k8 gauges save 13,000 primitives
body:
A simultaneous constant dyadic gauge on 218 eligible helpers reduces the selected-at-base PR1094 k8 scalar word by **13,000 primitives per complex invocation in each orientation**, including all added entry/exit work:

| Orientation | Baseline | Candidate |
|---|---:|---:|
| Forward | 149,002 | 136,002 |
| Backward | 149,018 | 136,018 |

**Status: finite scalar construction; no new kappa.** Paid recursive events and profiles are identical. Every original SCALE, ADD operand/order, frame and source-access operation is preserved; the 436 added boundary scales cost 630 real primitives per component. The complete primitive price includes coefficient-work initialization and clearing. All 712 symbolic input columns preserve the required map and arbitrary helper dirt. Local positive-prefix bounds remain 52/68 bits; conservative denominator depths change 22→24 forward and stay 26 backward. The retained local charge remains 192 bits; this is not revised global precision admission.

This extends @woklerx's **PR1161** one-helper constant gauge and Hanson Sun / @bbMisk's **PR1214** at-most-two-helper optimum. The new search considers all 237 eligible cold/FULL, unwrapped, no-COPY/clear helpers jointly. Four deterministic seed-29 starts terminate at exact coordinate stationarity; **no global optimum is claimed**. Shared ADD interactions are counted once, so this is not a sum of individual savings. The original donor assigns seed29 to complex supplier work; TASK.json explicitly marks the newer recursive-inventory card as changed to this scalar side result.

Only `research/k8-many-dyadic-seed29/` is added. Exact base: `dadfea6e8a78ff6ba901705f87532a71c6f5bbb8`. Source pins authenticate the actual PR1094 provider, PR1042 alias, and lowerer. PR1161 code is retained byte-identically with its attribution; the separately written checker imports only Sagar Thakrar's retained PR696 lowerer.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and its standard library:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/k8-many-dyadic-seed29
```

Expected: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/k8-many-dyadic-seed29 outcome=completed`.

Validation passes locally on macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.13 and 3.14.7:

- Complete certificate and all-712-column endpoints; independent rational-ratio reconstruction, literal primitive counts, six dirty-state fixtures and exact positive envelopes.
- Independent all-integer one-coordinate check: 2,036 evaluations per orientation with outward-tail justification.
- Five package test groups, including 13 endpoint/domain/package rejections, shared-edge and unit-discount controls, and optimized isolated relocation to a path containing spaces.
- Registered replay, metadata/source pins, 20 repository research tests (one expected skip), 25 selected-result tests, selected-record integrity and staged whitespace checks.

Native C++/complete hosted/controller admission, the selected cold replay, a global gauge optimum, remote CI success, and a formal multiplication theorem are not claimed. Compiler/all-size, realization, hosting, precision/tape, analytic and bit-interface assumptions remain inherited. README and TASK.json provide concrete next questions.

The final overlap refresh covered 854 open PR bodies and 11 discussions. [Discussion1258](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1258) records this scope. Sagar Thakrar's concurrent **PR1259** studies a time-varying gauge on one helper; this contribution uses a constant gauge on many helpers and neither imports nor combines that result. PR1170's stage-SCALE consolidation is also not composed.

Credit @woklerx, Hanson Sun, Sagar Thakrar, icekylinx, Jeremy Kothe, Rohan Arun, Douglas Colkitt and the retained supplier/hosting lineage. Prepared for **Philipp (@mightyOil)** with substantial **GPT-6 Astra / OpenAI Codex** assistance in research, proof, code, verification and writing. No independent human review or literature-priority claim. Apache-2.0; inherited notices retained.
